scenes.tts: A count comes out low. Were the missing neurons never made, or made and then lost?
scenes.visual: Title card: Count Across Time. One short bar labelled final count, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: A count comes out low. Were the missing neurons never made, or made and then lost?

scenes.tts: In nineteen thirty-four, Viktor Hamburger removed one wing bud from chick embryos about three days old.
scenes.caption: In 1934, Viktor Hamburger removed one wing bud from chick embryos about three days old.
scenes.visual: Schematic chick embryo; one wing bud, the small swelling on the flank, is removed. Credit: Hamburger, 1934.
scenes.narration: In 1934, Viktor Hamburger removed one wing bud from chick embryos about three days old.

scenes.tts: Days later, the operated side had fewer motor neurons than the intact side, its control.
scenes.visual: Spinal cord cross-section: fewer dots on the operated side than on the intact side, which is labelled control.
scenes.narration: Days later, the operated side had fewer motor neurons than the intact side, its control.

scenes.tts: Hamburger read this as the limb setting how many neurons the cord makes.
scenes.visual: Arrow from limb back to the cord, labelled: sets how many are made? (Hamburger's reading).
scenes.narration: Hamburger read this as the limb setting how many neurons the cord makes.

scenes.tts: That reading fits the count. So do others. Think of a bakery whose shelf ends the day half empty.
scenes.visual: A bakery shelf, half empty.
scenes.narration: That reading fits the count. So do others. Think of a bakery whose shelf ends the day half empty.

scenes.tts: It might have baked fewer, sent some away, or baked some as rolls.
scenes.visual: Three small shelves appear: baked fewer; sent away; came out as rolls.
scenes.narration: It might have baked fewer, sent some away, or baked some as rolls.

scenes.tts: Or it baked a full batch and threw half away. The shelf looks the same every time.
scenes.visual: A fourth shelf: thrown out. All four collapse into one identical half-empty shelf.
scenes.narration: Or it baked a full batch and threw half away. The shelf looks the same every time.

scenes.tts: A low neuron count is that shelf. A count made only at the end cannot tell the histories apart.
scenes.visual: The shelf becomes the short bar: operated side, final count.
scenes.narration: A low neuron count is that shelf. A count made only at the end cannot tell the histories apart.

scenes.tts: Pause, and predict. What would you count, and when, to tell never made from made and then lost?
scenes.visual: A blank time axis appears with the prompt: Pause and sketch.
scenes.narration: Pause, and predict. What would you count, and when, to tell never made from made and then lost?

scenes.tts: Count at closely spaced stages, on both sides. Count healthy neurons, and count dying ones.
scenes.visual: Tick marks along the time axis, one per stage. Two columns of counts: healthy, dying.
scenes.narration: Count at closely spaced stages, on both sides. Count healthy neurons, and count dying ones.

scenes.tts: A dying neuron often has a small, dark, condensed nucleus. It is called pick-nottick.
scenes.caption: A dying neuron often has a small, dark, condensed nucleus. It is called pyknotic.
scenes.visual: Close-up of a pyknotic nucleus. Label: pyknotic nucleus, often a dying cell.
scenes.narration: A dying neuron often has a small, dark, condensed nucleus. It is called pyknotic.

scenes.tts: Never made: the operated side never catches up, and no extra dying cells appear.
scenes.visual: Curve 1, never made: below the intact-side reference throughout. No red hump. Label: predicted under reduced production.
scenes.narration: Never made: the operated side never catches up, and no extra dying cells appear.

scenes.tts: But dying cells are cleared fast. So count often, and birth-date the cells, before trusting a missing hump.
scenes.caption: But dying cells are cleared fast. So count often, and birthdate the cells, before trusting a missing hump.
scenes.visual: Small inset: a pyknotic cell engulfed and gone between two tick marks. Label: a missing hump is not proof on its own.
scenes.narration: But dying cells are cleared fast. So count often, and birthdate the cells, before trusting a missing hump.

scenes.tts: Made, then lost: the sides start equal. Then dying cells appear, and the count falls behind.
scenes.visual: Curve 2, made then lost: equal at first, then falling, with a red hump of pyknotic nuclei beneath the fall. Schematic, not data.
scenes.narration: Made, then lost: the sides start equal. Then dying cells appear, and the count falls behind.

scenes.tts: In wartime Italy, Rita Levi Montal-cheeni and Giuseppe Levi studied staged sections like these, in a laboratory at home.
scenes.caption: In wartime Italy, Rita Levi-Montalcini and Giuseppe Levi studied staged sections like these, in a laboratory at home.
scenes.visual: Schematic, silver-stained-style neurons, not the original sections. Label: schematic. Credit: Levi-Montalcini and Levi, Turin and Piedmont, 1942 to 1944. A row of embryos at successive stages.
scenes.narration: In wartime Italy, Rita Levi-Montalcini and Giuseppe Levi studied staged sections like these, in a laboratory at home.

scenes.tts: They found neurons that had already formed, and were now degenerating. The missing neurons had been made.
scenes.visual: Differentiated neurons shown breaking down. Label: made, then lost.
scenes.narration: They found neurons that had already formed, and were now degenerating. The missing neurons had been made.

scenes.tts: In nineteen forty-nine, her joint paper with Hamburger, on the sensory neurons of chick spinal ganglia, supported that reading.
scenes.caption: In 1949, her joint paper with Hamburger, on the sensory neurons of chick spinal ganglia, supported that reading.
scenes.visual: Caption: 1949, St. Louis. A spinal ganglion of sensory neurons beside the cord, filling and then thinning across stages.
scenes.narration: In 1949, her joint paper with Hamburger, on the sensory neurons of chick spinal ganglia, supported that reading.

scenes.tts: The target's main job was not to call neurons into existence. It was to keep them alive.
scenes.visual: Card: not to make neurons, but to keep them alive.
scenes.narration: The target's main job was not to call neurons into existence. It was to keep them alive.

scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy-five, Hamburger counted the death itself, in normal embryos with all their limbs.
scenes.caption: In 1975, Hamburger counted the death itself, in normal embryos with all their limbs.
scenes.visual: Credit: Hamburger, 1975. A count-against-day axis for the lumbar lateral motor column.
scenes.narration: In 1975, Hamburger counted the death itself, in normal embryos with all their limbs.

scenes.tts: The leg's motor neurons peaked near day six. Then about two in five of them died, most within three days.
scenes.caption: The leg's motor neurons peaked near day 6. Then about two in five of them died, most within three days.
scenes.visual: The curve rises to just over 20,000 near day 6 and falls to about 12,000 after day 9.5. Shaded window: days 6.5 to 9.5. Label: about 40% of the peak lost.
scenes.narration: The leg's motor neurons peaked near day 6. Then about two in five of them died, most within three days.

scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy-six, Margaret Hollyday and Hamburger grafted an extra leg beside the normal one.
scenes.caption: In 1976, Margaret Hollyday and Hamburger grafted an extra leg beside the normal one.
scenes.visual: Credit: Hollyday and Hamburger, 1976. Schematic embryo with an extra leg grafted beside the normal leg.
scenes.narration: In 1976, Margaret Hollyday and Hamburger grafted an extra leg beside the normal one.

scenes.tts: Predict. If more target meant more births, where would the grafted side's count be at day six?
scenes.caption: Predict. If more target meant more births, where would the grafted side's count be at day 6?
scenes.visual: Two predicted curves are drawn faintly: more births, higher from day 6; fewer deaths, equal at day 6 and higher later. Prompt: Pause and sketch.
scenes.narration: Predict. If more target meant more births, where would the grafted side's count be at day 6?

scenes.tts: At day six, before the normal loss, the grafted side had no more motor neurons than the control.
scenes.caption: At day 6, before the normal loss, the grafted side had no more motor neurons than the control.
scenes.visual: The real result is drawn over the predictions: equal at day 6.
scenes.narration: At day 6, before the normal loss, the grafted side had no more motor neurons than the control.

scenes.tts: Later, in embryos whose grafts moved vigorously, it had more. About a tenth to over a quarter more.
scenes.visual: The grafted-side curve sits above the control after the death window. Label: about 11% to 28% more, in embryos whose grafts moved vigorously. Schematic, not data.
scenes.narration: Later, in embryos whose grafts moved vigorously, it had more. About a tenth to over a quarter more.

scenes.tts: More target did not mean more births. It meant fewer deaths.
scenes.visual: Card: not more births, fewer deaths.
scenes.narration: More target did not mean more births. It meant fewer deaths.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: a count tells you a history only if you also counted along the way.
scenes.visual: Closing card: A count tells you a history only if you also counted along the way.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: a count tells you a history only if you also counted along the way.
